articles.title: AI firms must answer for rogue bots, says boss of hacked company
articles.summary: Clement Delangue said he didn't want cyber attacks on other companies to become "normalised".
articles.titleZh: 被黑公司老板表示，人工智能公司必须对流氓机器人负责
articles.summaryZh: 克莱门特·德兰格表示，他不希望针对其他公司的网络攻击变得“常态化”。

contentParagraphs.en: The boss of one of the companies recently hacked by out-of-control artificial intelligence (AI) says bot makers must be accountable for cyber attacks carried out by their creations.Clement Delangue's company Hugging Face was breached by a rogue OpenAI bot that broke out of a test environment and autonomously attacked his firm earlier this month.Hugging Face had to rebuild around a third of its IT network after the unprecedented incident.He told CNN his company - which is a small start-up - will not be taking legal action against OpenAI, but added that these types of hacks are illegal and should remain so."Everyone has to remember that a cyber-attack is a crime and it is illegal," he said.Delangue said he hoped legal frameworks would ensure the companies that make mistakes leading to the hacks are "accountable."He added that he didn't want cyber attacks on other companies to become "normalised".His remarks come after Anthrophic, the maker of the chat bot Claude, also admitted that its bot had attacked three companies in similar circumstances in recent months.Anthropic revealed on Friday that it only realised its bot had escaped the containment system and hacked the organisations after doing a review prompted by the recent OpenAI incident.In both cases neither of the artificial intelligence giants knew that their models had roamed the internet attacking companies until long after the attacks had been carried out.The AI models were being tested on their hacking skills and carried out the attacks by breaking out of seemingly secure "sandboxes" to search the internet for ways to complete the tasks set by researchers. The unprecedented incidents have sparked fierce debates in the cyber-security and legal world about who, if anybody, should be held liable for attacks by out-of-control AI agents."Agentic security failures unfold at machine speed, but determining who is materially liable still moves at a lawsuit's pace," said Dor Sarig, co-founder and Chief Builder at Pillar Security.Sarig was concerned that accountability is already becoming "ambiguous". "Today the industry is extending grace, but the first time an autonomous agent causes a breach involving real data, a real plaintiff, and real financial losses, liability won't be an academic debate anymore," he said. "That's when the legal framework, and not just the technical safeguards, will be stress-tested."
contentParagraphs.zh: 最近遭受失控人工智能 (AI) 黑客攻击的一家公司的老板表示，机器人制造商必须为其创造的网络攻击负责。克莱门特·德兰格 (Clement Delangue) 的公司 Hugging Face 被一个流氓 OpenAI 机器人入侵，该机器人本月早些时候突破了测试环境并自主攻击了他的公司。在这场史无前例的事件发生后，Hugging Face 不得不重建大约三分之一的 IT 网络。他告诉 CNN，他的公司（一家小型初创企业）不会采取法律行动他说，“每个人都必须记住，网络攻击是一种犯罪，而且是非法的。”Delangue 表示，他希望法律框架能够确保犯错导致黑客攻击的公司“承担责任”。他补充说，他不希望针对其他公司的网络攻击变得“常态化”。在他发表上述言论之前，聊天机器人 Claude 的制造商 Anthrophic 也承认，其近几个月来，该机器人曾在类似情况下攻击过三家公司。Anthropic 周五透露，在对最近的 OpenAI 事件进行审查后，它才意识到其机器人已逃离遏制系统并入侵了这些组织。在这两种情况下，直到攻击发生很久之后，这两家人工智能巨头才知道他们的模型已经在互联网上漫游攻击公司。人工智能模型正在测试其黑客技能，并通过突破看似安全的“沙箱”来进行攻击，以在互联网上搜索完成攻击的方法。研究人员设定的任务。这些史无前例的事件在网络安全和法律界引发了激烈的争论，争论的焦点是谁应该为失控的人工智能代理的攻击负责。“代理安全故障以机器的速度展开，但确定谁应该承担重大责任仍然以诉讼的速度进行，”Pillar Security 联合创始人兼首席构建者多尔·萨里格 (Dor Sarig) 表示。萨里格担心责任已经变得“模糊”。他说：“今天，该行业正在给予宽限，但当自主代理第一次造成涉及真实数据、真实原告和真实财务损失的泄露时，责任将不再是学术争论。” “届时，法律框架而不仅仅是技术保障措施将受到压力测试。”

articles.title: BP puts North Sea business up for sale
articles.summary: The decision follows a review of BP's operations and is set to end 60 years of production in the region by the oil giant.
articles.titleZh: 英国石油公司 (BP) 出售北海业务
articles.summaryZh: 该决定是在对 BP 的运营进行审查后作出的，该决定将结束这家石油巨头在该地区 60 年的生产。

contentParagraphs.en: BP has said it is putting its North Sea business up for sale in a move that would end 60 years of production in the region by the oil giant.The decision follows a review of BP's operations as it seeks to slim down the group. Its North Sea business has five production hubs - two in the central North Sea and three west of Shetland - and employs about 1,100 people.Earlier this week, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he told US President Donald Trump he would take a "pragmatic approach" to the issue of North Sea oil and gas.Trump, some trade unions, industry figures and some Labour MPs all back increased drilling in the North Sea."The UK has been our home for more than 100 years and will continue to play an important role in our future," BP chief executive Meg O'Neill said."We're proud of the jobs we create, the contribution we make to the UK economy, and the work we do to keep energy flowing every day," she said.The company said it remained committed to operating the business safely and reliably throughout the sale process.Its North Sea business produced 117,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day in 2025, a small fraction of the oil giant's 2.3 million barrels of daily production.The North Sea has increasingly become a topic for political debate.In its 2024 general election manifesto, Labour said it would not issue new licences for drilling, but would honour existing ones.But in recent months, as the Iran war pushed up global oil prices, calls have grown for more North Sea drilling to be approved, from the Conservatives, Reform UK and from President Trump, while also becoming a divisive issue within the Labour party.Some Labour MPs have urged the government to take a more liberal approach, warning that the transition away from oil and gas must protect jobs and the cost of energy bills.But others have backed the government's existing approach, arguing that expanding renewable energy is key to improving energy security and reducing the impact on climate change.As energy secretary in Sir Keir Starmer's government, Ed Miliband was a staunch supporter of the manifesto position. Miliband is now the foreign secretary in Burnham's government.Burnham himself has seemingly left the door open to future drilling. He said he told President Trump this week: "There is a resource there. When people are struggling - you can't ignore that."Labour's deputy leader Lucy Powell previously told the BBC that Burnham would stick to the party's manifesto commitments, but there would be a "change of emphasis" on North Sea oil and gas.Oil and gas companies have also criticised the UK's windfall tax, which they argue means the North Sea has lost some of its appeal in recent years.
contentParagraphs.zh: 英国石油公司(BP)表示，将出售其北海业务，此举将结束这家石油巨头在该地区长达60年的生产业务。该决定是在英国石油公司(BP)寻求精简集团业务之际对业务进行审查之后做出的。其北海业务拥有五个生产中心，其中两个位于北海中部，三个位于设得兰群岛西部，拥有约 1,100 名员工。本周早些时候，英国首相安迪·伯纳姆表示，他告诉美国总统唐纳德·特朗普，他将对北海石油和天然气问题采取“务实的态度”。特朗普、一些工会、行业人士和一些工党议员都支持增加在北海的钻探活动。英国石油公司首席执行官梅格·奥尼尔表示：“我们对我们创造的就业机会、对英国经济做出的贡献以及我们为保持能源每天流动所做的工作感到自豪。”该公司表示，在整个销售过程中仍致力于安全可靠地运营业务。2025年，其北海业务每天生产117,000桶油当量，这只是这家石油巨头每天2.3油当量的一小部分。日产量百万桶。北海日益成为政治辩论的话题。工党在2024年大选宣言中表示，不会发放新的钻探许可证，但会尊重现有许可证。但近几个月来，随着伊朗战争推高全球油价，保守党、改革英国和特朗普总统要求批准更多北海钻探的呼声越来越高，同时也成为工党内部的一个分裂问题。一些工党议员敦促政府采取更加自由的态度，警告说，摆脱石油和天然气的转型必须保护就业和能源费用。但其他人支持政府现有的做法，认为扩大可再生能源是改善能源安全和减少对气候变化影响的关键。作为基尔·斯塔默爵士政府的能源部长，埃德·米利班德是宣言立场的坚定支持者。米利班德现在是伯纳姆政府的外交大臣。伯纳姆本人似乎已经为未来的钻探敞开了大门。他说，他本周告诉特朗普总统：“那里有资源。当人们陷入困境时，你不能忽视这一点。”工党副党魁露西·鲍威尔此前告诉英国广播公司，伯纳姆将坚持该党的宣言承诺，但对北海石油和天然气的“重点将发生改变”。石油和天然气公司也批评了英国的暴利税，他们认为这意味着北海近年来失去了一些吸引力。

articles.title: Drought conditions may worsen before improving as little rain in sight
articles.summary: Conditions in the most parched areas of the United Kingdom could worsen before they improve, according to the latest forecasts.
articles.titleZh: 由于看不到降雨，干旱状况在改善之前可能会恶化
articles.summaryZh: 根据最新预测，英国最干旱地区的情况在好转之前可能会进一步恶化。

contentParagraphs.en: Parts of the UK can expect to see some rain through Friday and into the weekend, though for the areas of England and Wales under drought conditions the coming days look set to remain dry.Friday will be rather cloudy across northern areas of the UK, with the chance of some scattered showers which may be locally rather heavy.Further south, though, it looks set to be another generally dry day with variable amounts of cloud and some sunny spells. South-east England, which is officially in drought, will have another warm day.Into the weekend, the dry weather looks set to continue for most, with the exception of Scotland, which may see some isolated showers across the far north.Next week, the forecast looks more unsettled, with more of a chance of rain, though it is likely to be northwestern parts of the UK which are the wettest. Some forecast models do suggest that more southern areas may receive some useful rain, but this is much less certain.Despite some rain in the forecast in the coming week, it will not be enough to end drought conditions.When rain falls in the summer months, high daytime temperatures can mean that the water quickly evaporates away from the soil. Meanwhile, a series of quick downpours such as heavy summer showers or thunderstorms may appear to give large rainfall totals, but the rain falls faster than the soil can absorb it.The ideal scenario is for rain to fall overnight to mitigate the loss from evaporation. However, to alleviate the drought there would still need to be a prolonged spell of rain over a number of days and weeks. This means the rain forecast in the coming days is likely to do very little to quench the parched earth.Wales has received just 8% of its long-term average rainfall for July, putting it on course to be the driest July there since records began 190 years ago.Rhian Thomas, Sustainable Water and Nature Manager at NRW, said: "The toll on the environment, our land and agriculture is clear to see, with many of our teams still dealing with the aftermath of extensive wildfires which have devastated forestry, grassland and special habitats."In England, July has brought just 7% of expected rainfall, falling to 1% across southern England.On Wednesday, the Environment Agency, warned that the hot and dry weather meant people are "using water faster than nature can replenish it".Heading into August, the forecast trend is for warmer- and drier-than-average weather, meaning drought conditions could worsen before they improve.
contentParagraphs.zh: 英国部分地区预计周五到周末都会有降雨，不过英格兰和威尔士地区处于干旱条件下，未来几天预计将保持干燥。周五英国北部地区将多云，可能会有零星阵雨，局部地区可能会相当大。不过，在更南部的地区，看起来将是又一个普遍干燥的日子，云量不等，偶尔会有晴朗天气。正式进入干旱状态的英格兰东南部将迎来又一个温暖的日子。进入周末，大多数地区的干燥天气似乎仍将持续，但苏格兰除外，远北地区可能会出现一些零星阵雨。下周，天气预报看起来更加不稳定，下雨的可能性更大，尽管英国西北部地区可能是最潮湿的地区。一些预测模型确实表明，更多的南部地区可能会收到一些有用的降雨，但这不太确定。尽管预测未来一周会出现一些降雨，但这还不足以结束干旱状况。当夏季降雨时，白天的高温可能意味着水分会迅速从土壤中蒸发。与此同时，一系列快速倾盆大雨，如夏季大阵雨或雷暴，可能会带来大量降雨总量，但降雨速度快于土壤的吸收速度。理想的情况是夜间降雨，以减轻蒸发损失。然而，为了缓解干旱，仍然需要持续数天和数周的长时间降雨。这意味着未来几天的降雨量可能无法缓解干旱的大地。威尔士 7 月份的降雨量仅为长期平均降雨量的 8%，这将是该州自 190 年前有记录以来最干燥的 7 月份。北威州可持续水和自然经理瑞安·托马斯 (Rhian Thomas) 表示：“对环境、土地和农业造成的损失是显而易见的，我们的许多团队仍在处理大范围野火的后果，森林、草原和特殊栖息地遭到破坏。“在英格兰，7月份的降雨量仅为预期的7%，英格兰南部地区的降雨量降至1%。周三，环境署警告说，炎热干燥的天气意味着人们“用水的速度快于自然补充水的速度”。进入8月，预测趋势是天气比平均水平更温暖和干燥，这意味着干旱状况在改善之前可能会恶化。

articles.title: Over 81,000 U.S. soldiers are missing from past wars. One may soon be identified
articles.summary: In June, the Department of Defense disinterred the remains of an unidentified WWII soldier who had been buried in Sitka, Alaska for decades. Now, they'll try to confirm who he is.
articles.titleZh: 超过 81,000 名美国士兵在过去的战争中失踪。其中之一可能很快就会被识别出来
articles.summaryZh: 六月，国防部挖掘出一具身份不明的二战士兵的遗骸，该士兵已被埋葬在阿拉斯加锡特卡数十年。现在，他们将尝试确认他是谁。

contentParagraphs.en: The headstone of an unidentified soldier known as "X-3" is marked as "Unknown" at the Sitka National Cemetery in Sitka, Alaska.
contentParagraphs.zh: 在阿拉斯加州锡特卡国家公墓，一名被称为“X-3”的身份不明的士兵的墓碑被标记为“未知”。

contentParagraphs.en: Hope McKenney/KCAW
contentParagraphs.zh: 霍普·麦肯尼/KCAW

contentParagraphs.en: Hope McKenney/KCAW
contentParagraphs.zh: 霍普·麦肯尼/KCAW

contentParagraphs.en: Back in June, a dozen service members, veterans, and police and fire personnel stood at solemn salute in the small island community of Sitka, Alaska while two U.S. Coast Guardsmen carried an American flag-adorned case from a cemetery to a hearse.
contentParagraphs.zh: 早在六月，十几名军人、退伍军人、警察和消防人员在阿拉斯加锡特卡的小岛社区庄严敬礼，两名美国海岸警卫队人员将一个装饰着美国国旗的箱子从墓地抬到灵车上。

contentParagraphs.en: They weren't there to honor a recently deceased soldier. Rather, to formally mark the disinterment and transport of an unidentified soldier known simply as "X-3," who's been dead for over eighty years.
contentParagraphs.zh: 他们来这里不是为了纪念最近去世的士兵。相反，是为了正式纪念一名身份不明的士兵的挖掘和运输，这名士兵简称为“X-3”，他已经去世八十多年了。

contentParagraphs.en: X-3 is one of more than 81,000 U.S. service members whose remains have either never been found or never been identified. The majority are missing from World War II, the Vietnam War, and the Korean War.
contentParagraphs.zh: X-3 是 81,000 多名美国军人之一，他们的遗体要么从未被发现，要么从未得到确认。大多数人在第二次世界大战、越南战争和朝鲜战争中失踪。

contentParagraphs.en: An agency within the Department of Defense is tasked with locating and identifying these service members. Their remains are rarely found on U.S. soil because it wasn't a primary theater of war, according to DOD. But in Hawaii and Alaska, where military action took place during WWII, there are more missing soldiers. DOD says there are currently around 120 unidentified soldiers in Alaska and over 1,900 in Hawaii.
contentParagraphs.zh: 国防部内的一个机构负责定位和识别这些军人。据国防部称，他们的遗骸很少在美国境内发现，因为美国不是主要战场。但在二战期间发生军事行动的夏威夷和阿拉斯加，失踪士兵更多。国防部表示，目前阿拉斯加约有 120 名身份不明的士兵，夏威夷有超过 1,900 名士兵。

contentParagraphs.en: The remains of the unidentified solder known as "X-3" are loaded into a hearse in Sitka, Alaska before being transported to a Midwest forensics lab.
contentParagraphs.zh: 被称为“X-3”的身份不明的焊料残骸被装载到阿拉斯加锡特卡的灵车上，然后被运送到中西部的法医实验室。

contentParagraphs.en: Hope McKenney/KCAW
contentParagraphs.zh: 霍普·麦肯尼/KCAW

contentParagraphs.en: Hope McKenney/KCAW
contentParagraphs.zh: 霍普·麦肯尼/KCAW

contentParagraphs.en: A plane crash in the Aleutians
contentParagraphs.zh: 阿留申群岛发生飞机失事

contentParagraphs.en: The story of X-3 goes back to June 3, 1942, when Japan bombed Unalaska — also known as Dutch Harbor — a community about 800 air miles from Anchorage in the Aleutian Islands. The U.S. military responded, sending resources to help defend against the attack.
contentParagraphs.zh: X-3 的故事可以追溯到 1942 年 6 月 3 日，当时日本轰炸了乌纳拉斯卡（也称为荷兰港），这是距离阿留申群岛安克雷奇约 800 英里的一个社区。美国军方做出回应，派遣资源帮助防御袭击。

contentParagraphs.en: "One of the planes crashed outside of Cold Bay, on the north side of the Alaska Peninsula. All the service members on that plane perished," said Michael Livingston, a local history buff who's spent a lot of time studying WWII events in the Aleutians.
contentParagraphs.zh: “其中一架飞机在阿拉斯加半岛北侧的科尔德湾外坠毁。飞机上的所有军人都丧生，”当地历史爱好者迈克尔·利文斯顿（Michael Livingston）说，他花了很多时间研究阿留申群岛的二战事件。

contentParagraphs.en: Sixteen soldiers were on the twin-motor C-53B when it went down during a routine flight between two Alaska bases. The wreckage of the plane and 10 of the servicemen were never found. Livingston said a local fur trapper found the bodies of the other six soldiers after they washed up on shore and buried them temporarily. The U.S. military then re-buried them in a local cemetery. And then, after the war, moved most of them to their respective communities. Only one of the recovered men remained unidentified: X-3.
contentParagraphs.zh: 这架双发动机 C-53B 在往返两个阿拉斯加基地的例行飞行中坠毁，机上载有 16 名士兵。飞机残骸和 10 名军人至今仍未找到。利文斯顿说，当地毛皮捕猎者发现了其他六名士兵的尸体，他们被冲上岸并暂时埋葬。美军随后将他们重新埋葬在当地的一个墓地。然后，战争结束后，他们中的大多数人搬到了各自的社区。只有一名被救出的人身份不明：X-3。

contentParagraphs.en: "He was moved to Sitka," Livingston said. "We've been trying to get X-3 identified for a long time."
contentParagraphs.zh: “他被转移到锡特卡，”利文斯顿说。 “长期以来，我们一直在努力查明 X-3 的身份。”

contentParagraphs.en: For years, Livingston advocated for DOD to disinter X-3 and try to identify him, but was unsuccessful.
contentParagraphs.zh: 多年来，利文斯顿一直主张国防部挖掘 X-3 并试图识别他的身份，但没有成功。

contentParagraphs.en: A photo of 2nd Lt. Eugene Christensen of Nebraska.
contentParagraphs.zh: 内布拉斯加州第二中尉尤金·克里斯滕森的照片。

contentParagraphs.en: Photo Courtesy of Chris Pfeiffer
contentParagraphs.zh: 照片由克里斯·菲佛提供

contentParagraphs.en: Photo Courtesy of Chris Pfeiffer
contentParagraphs.zh: 照片由克里斯·菲佛提供

contentParagraphs.en: "Could it be my uncle? Yes. Could it not be? Yes."
contentParagraphs.zh: “难道是我舅舅？是的。难道不是吗？是的。”

contentParagraphs.en: Meanwhile, in Texas, 71-year-old Chris Pfeiffer had also spent years trying to figure out what had happened to his grandmother's brother, who was one of the men who went down on that flight.
contentParagraphs.zh: 与此同时，在德克萨斯州，71 岁的克里斯·菲弗 (Chris Pfeiffer) 也花了数年时间试图弄清楚他祖母的兄弟发生了什么事，他是那架航班上坠机的人之一。

contentParagraphs.en: "We've always known that we lost a great uncle in the Aleutian Islands," Pfeiffer said. "And here we are, 83 years later."
contentParagraphs.zh: “我们一直都知道我们在阿留申群岛失去了一位叔祖父，”菲弗说。 “83 年后，我们来到了这里。”

contentParagraphs.en: Pfeiffer believes his great uncle – 2nd Lt. Eugene Christensen of Nebraska — is X-3. According to Pfieffer, Christensen went to college for just one year before he enlisted in the U.S. Army Air Forces (the predecessor of the U.S. Air Force) at age 21. He spent less than a year in the Army before his plane went down.
contentParagraphs.zh: 菲弗相信他的叔公——内布拉斯加州的尤金·克里斯滕森中尉——是 X-3。据普菲弗介绍，克里斯滕森只上过一年大学，21 岁时就加入了美国陆军空军（美国空军的前身）。在陆军服役不到一年，他的飞机就坠毁了。

contentParagraphs.en: Pfeiffer, a military vet himself, has collected hundreds of pages of records about the crash and his great uncle over the years, and, like Livingston, petitioned DOD to disinter the remains.
contentParagraphs.zh: 菲弗本人也是一名退伍军人，多年来收集了数百页有关坠机事件和他叔祖父的记录，并且像利文斯顿一样，请求国防部挖掘遗骸。

contentParagraphs.en: He said he's hopeful, but also realistic.
contentParagraphs.zh: 他说他充满希望，但也很现实。

contentParagraphs.en: "Could it be my uncle? Yes. Could it not be? Yes. We have to manage our expectations on this," he said.
contentParagraphs.zh: “会是我叔叔吗？是的。难道不是吗？是的。我们必须管理我们对此的期望，”他说。

contentParagraphs.en: Pfeiffer said his great-grandparents, parents, and other relatives passed away without ever knowing what happened to Christensen, and he wishes the disinterment had been approved sooner.
contentParagraphs.zh: 菲弗说，他的曾祖父母、父母和其他亲戚去世时都不知道克里斯滕森发生了什么事，他希望挖掘工作能早点获得批准。

contentParagraphs.en: "It could have been shared," he said. "There's some closure, because now we know this is the one opportunity, it's the best one we have, to see what happened."
contentParagraphs.zh: “它本来可以分享，”他说。 “事情已经结束了，因为现在我们知道这是唯一的机会，也是我们拥有的最好的机会，看看到底发生了什么。”

contentParagraphs.en: Aaron Cummings is a senior planner with the Defense POW/MIA Accounting Agency (DPAA), the DOD agency in charge of recovering and identifying missing service members. Cummings said the DPAA has been looking into this case since 2017, but progress stalled until Pfeiffer got involved.
contentParagraphs.zh: 亚伦·卡明斯 (Aaron Cummings) 是国防部战俘/失踪人员会计局 (DPAA) 的高级规划师，该机构是国防部负责寻找和识别失踪军人的机构。卡明斯表示，DPAA 自 2017 年以来一直在调查此案，但在 Pfeiffer 介入之前进展陷入停滞。

contentParagraphs.en: "We are an agency with finite resources," he said. "It's hard to prioritize, it's hard to rack and stack your missions, and family interest is one of the elements that we utilize to determine how we prioritize and which missions move up the ladder."
contentParagraphs.zh: “我们是一个资源有限的机构，”他说。 “很难确定优先顺序，也很难安排和堆叠你的任务，而家庭利益是我们用来确定如何确定优先顺序以及哪些任务升级的因素之一。”

contentParagraphs.en: Workers from DOD and Veterans Affairs disinter the remains of "X-3."
contentParagraphs.zh: 国防部和退伍军人事务部的工作人员正在挖掘“X-3”的遗骸。

contentParagraphs.en: Hope McKenney/KCAW
contentParagraphs.zh: 霍普·麦肯尼/KCAW

contentParagraphs.en: Hope McKenney/KCAW
contentParagraphs.zh: 霍普·麦肯尼/KCAW

contentParagraphs.en: Unique and challenging disinterment
contentParagraphs.zh: 独特且具有挑战性的发掘

contentParagraphs.en: Over several days in late June, a recovery team from DPAA, including an archeologist, odontologist (dental expert), a medic, and Cummings, hand dug the grave of X-3, which was perched on a narrow step of the main hill at the national cemetery.
contentParagraphs.zh: 6 月下旬的几天里，DPAA 的一个修复小组，包括一名考古学家、牙科医生（牙科专家）、一名医务人员和卡明斯，手工挖掘了 X-3 的坟墓，该坟墓坐落在国家公墓主山的一个狭窄台阶上。

contentParagraphs.en: Cummings said the dig was unique in many ways. They were concerned that the casket, which has lain in Sitka's rain-drenched soil since 1948, might have shifted due to subsurface movement. The team tried excavating another unknown soldier from an unrelated case just a day before, but were unsuccessful. Cummings said they dug 10 feet below the surface, but found the grave empty. He said they were fortunate to find X-3's remains just three feet under.
contentParagraphs.zh: 卡明斯表示，这次挖掘在很多方面都是独一无二的。自 1948 年以来，棺材一直躺在锡特卡被雨水浸湿的土壤中，他们担心棺材可能会因地下运动而发生移动。就在一天前，该小组试图从一个无关的案件中挖掘出另一名无名士兵，但没有成功。卡明斯说，他们在地表以下挖了 10 英尺，但发现坟墓是空的。他说他们很幸运在水下三英尺处发现了 X-3 的遗骸。

contentParagraphs.en: "It was a very successful, respectful, and honorable extraction. We had challenges with X-3, but ultimate success," he said.
contentParagraphs.zh: “这是一次非常成功、受人尊敬和光荣的撤离。我们在 X-3 方面遇到了挑战，但最终取得了成功，”他说。

contentParagraphs.en: Fortunately, he said, the remains were intact, preserved in a wooden casket lined with metal.
contentParagraphs.zh: 他说，幸运的是，遗骸完好无损，保存在一个衬有金属的木棺中。

contentParagraphs.en: Now that X-3's remains have been disinterred, Cummings said their job is to combine the hi
contentParagraphs.zh: 现在 X-3 的遗体已经被挖掘出来，卡明斯说他们的工作就是将这些遗骸结合起来。

articles.title: Google pauses AI satellite images, after fears of deepfakes in the sky
articles.summary: Journalists, human rights advocates and open source analysts recoiled in horror at the initial decision: "The opportunities for abuse and disinfo are literally boundless," said one.
articles.titleZh: 由于担心天空中存在深度造假，谷歌暂停了人工智能卫星图像
articles.summaryZh: 记者、人权倡导者和开源分析师对最初的决定感到恐惧：“滥用和虚假信息的机会实际上是无限的，”其中一位人士表示。

contentParagraphs.en: An AI-generated image showing multiple fires on and near Kharg Island, an Iranian island in the Persian Gulf that is home to a strategic oil terminal.
contentParagraphs.zh: 人工智能生成的图像显示哈格岛及其附近发生多起火灾，哈格岛是波斯湾的伊朗岛屿，是一个战略石油码头的所在地。

contentParagraphs.en: A day after Google unveiled a new feature that allowed users to create AI-generated satellite images with the click of a button on its Google Earth platform, the company announced it was removing the tool.
contentParagraphs.zh: 谷歌推出一项新功能，允许用户通过点击谷歌地球平台上的按钮来创建人工智能生成的卫星图像，一天后，该公司宣布将删除该工具。

contentParagraphs.en: "We've seen geospatial professionals using this feature for a range of useful purposes," Google said in a statement on X. "However we've also seen people sharing screenshots of generated imagery that appear to violate our policies. So we're rolling back this feature in Google Earth while we work on implementing stronger guardrails."
contentParagraphs.zh: 谷歌在 X 的一份声明中表示：“我们已经看到地理空间专业人士将这一功能用于一系列有用的目的。但是，我们也看到人们分享了似乎违反我们政策的生成图像的屏幕截图。因此，我们正在回滚 Google 地球中的这一功能，同时我们致力于实施更强大的护栏。”

contentParagraphs.en: In its initial announcement of the new feature on Thursday, the company said it was designed to work with users' imaginations: "Just zoom in to a place in Google Earth on web (sic), tap 'create image,' and type whatever you want to see," Bryan Horowitz, a product manager wrote.
contentParagraphs.zh: 在周四首次宣布这项新功能时，该公司表示，该功能旨在满足用户的想象力：“只需放大到网络版 Google 地球（原文如此）中的某个位置，点击‘创建图像’，然后输入您想查看的任何内容，”产品经理 Bryan Horowitz 写道。

contentParagraphs.en: But for experts and analysts who rely on Google's imagery to verify breaking news and atrocities in hard-to-reach parts of the world, the potential to create deepfake satellite imagery at the click of a button was horrifying.
contentParagraphs.zh: 但对于依靠谷歌图像来验证世界上难以到达地区的突发新闻和暴行的专家和分析师来说，只需点击一个按钮即可创建深度伪造卫星图像的潜力是可怕的。

contentParagraphs.en: "I tried refugees at the Mexican border, a nuclear plant in Iran, a crash in Amsterdam, a hospital with a bomb crater in Gaza. Nothing was refused," Henk van Ess, an open-source researcher who first wrote about the potential damage the tool could cause, told NPR via text.
contentParagraphs.zh: “我尝试过墨西哥边境的难民、伊朗的核电站、阿姆斯特丹的坠机事件、加沙的一家有弹坑的医院。没有什么被拒绝的，”开源研究员 Henk van Ess 通过短信告诉 NPR，他是第一个撰写该工具可能造成的潜在损害的人。

contentParagraphs.en: NPR was able to easily generate images of Iran's Kharg Island on fire, and a flooded U.S. Capitol complex. Both events, which have not happened, would constitute major news if they were real.
contentParagraphs.zh: NPR 能够轻松生成伊朗哈格岛着火和美国国会大厦被淹的图像。这两件事虽然没有发生，但如果是真的，将构成重大新闻。

contentParagraphs.en: Online, journalists and open-source investigators wondered aloud about Google's decision. "Very curious how or if this idea was red teamed internally because the opportunities for abuse and disinfo are literally boundless," Evan Hill, an visual forensics investigator at the Washington Post wrote on X.
contentParagraphs.zh: 在网上，记者和开源调查人员对谷歌的决定表示好奇。 《华盛顿邮报》视觉取证调查员埃文·希尔 (Evan Hill) 在 X 上写道：“非常好奇这个想法是如何或是否在内部被红队考虑的，因为滥用和虚假信息的机会实际上是无限的。”

contentParagraphs.en: So it seems Google activated its AI image generation program inside its satellite image app today (blog post here: https://t.co/z7JlLrNuB8). Very curious how or if this idea was red teamed internally because the opportunities for abuse and disinfo are literally boundless. https://t.co/Dnjx3D1Gwr— Evan Hill (@evanhill) July 30, 2026
contentParagraphs.zh: 因此，谷歌今天似乎在其卫星图像应用程序中激活了人工智能图像生成程序（博客文章：https://t.co/z7JlLrNuB8）。非常好奇这个想法是如何或是否是内部红队的，因为滥用和虚假信息的机会实际上是无限的。 https://t.co/Dnjx3D1Gwr—埃文·希尔 (@evanhill) 2026 年 7 月 30 日

contentParagraphs.en: Eyes in the sky
contentParagraphs.zh: 眼睛在天空

contentParagraphs.en: As the online world fills with AI-generated deepfakes and slop, satellite imagery has been a key tool for understanding what's real and what's not. Open-source investigators have used satellite images to verify events on the ground, and as reference for understanding videos and images shared online.
contentParagraphs.zh: 随着网络世界充斥着人工智能生成的深度伪造品和虚假内容，卫星图像已成为了解真实和虚假的关键工具。开源调查人员使用卫星图像来验证地面事件，并作为理解在线共享的视频和图像的参考。

contentParagraphs.en: Google Earth imagery is not always the most up-to-date, but its sweeping, high-resolution coverage of the planet can provide important reference imagery for both images from the ground and more current images from other satellites.
contentParagraphs.zh: Google 地球图像并不总是最新的，但其对地球的全面、高分辨率覆盖可以为地面图像和其他卫星的最新图像提供重要的参考图像。

contentParagraphs.en: "Satellite imagery has been kind of a safe bet when it comes to verifying an event because it's hard to fake," says Jake Godin, a senior researcher with the online group Bellingcat, which does visual forensic investigations. Satellite images are usually controlled by companies or institutions, and their source, a camera hundreds of miles above the earth's surface, has historically been hard to imitate.
contentParagraphs.zh: 从事视觉取证调查的在线组织 Bellingcat 的高级研究员杰克·戈丁 (Jake Godin) 表示：“在验证事件时，卫星图像是一种安全的选择，因为它很难伪造。”卫星图像通常由公司或机构控制，其来源是距地球表面数百英里的摄像机，历来难以模仿。

contentParagraphs.en: Fakes from space
contentParagraphs.zh: 来自太空的赝品

contentParagraphs.en: Godin noted fake satellite imagery has already cropped up in limited cases. Early on in the U.S.-Israel war with Iran, for example, fake images circulated of a damaged U.S. base in Bahrain. The images, which popped up in Iranian media, appeared to use Google Earth images and Google AI to generate fake damage at the base. (Real satellite images later showed that the base was, in fact, damaged, just not in the way shown in the fake image.)
contentParagraphs.zh: 戈丁指出，虚假卫星图像已经在有限的情况下出现。例如，在美以与伊朗的战争初期，巴林美国基地受损的虚假图片就流传开来。这些出现在伊朗媒体上的图像似乎是使用谷歌地球图像和谷歌人工智能在基地制造假损坏。 （真实的卫星图像后来显示，基地实际上被损坏了，只是不像假图像中显示的那样。）

contentParagraphs.en: An AI-generated image showing significant flooding around the U.S. Capitol.
contentParagraphs.zh: 人工智能生成的图像显示美国国会大厦周围发生严重洪水。

contentParagraphs.en: Generated and annotated by NPR

contentParagraphs.en: But putting the tools together to create AI-generated satellite images with a single click has the potential to vastly accelerate the generation of AI fakes, Godin said. "It's just streamlining the process, which I think is going to make it proliferate more."
contentParagraphs.zh: 但戈丁说，将这些工具组合在一起，只需单击一下即可创建人工智能生成的卫星图像，有可能大大加速人工智能赝品的生成。 “这只是简化了流程，我认为这将使其更加普及。”

contentParagraphs.en: Godin worries that the spread of fake images will add to confusion and misinformation. "Misinformation travels further and faster than any sort of correction," he said. Moreover, governments will now be more likely to claim satellite images are fake, even if they are real, undermining public trust.
contentParagraphs.zh: 戈丁担心假图像的传播会加剧混乱和错误信息。 “错误信息比任何形式的纠正传播得更远、更快，”他说。此外，政府现在更有可能声称卫星图像是假的，即使它们是真实的，从而损害了公众的信任。

contentParagraphs.en: In an posting on X on Thursday, the company said it "takes misinformation seriously." The company noted that all images are marked with its SynthID watermark, which ensures it will be flagged as AI-generated in other Google tools such as Gemini. "In addition, we prevent image creation on harmful topics and are continually updating our protections," it said.
contentParagraphs.zh: 该公司周四在 X 上发布的一篇文章中表示，它“严肃对待错误信息”。该公司指出，所有图像都标有 SynthID 水印，这确保它将在 Gemini 等其他谷歌工具中被标记为人工智能生成。 “此外，我们会防止有害主题的图像创建，并不断更新我们的保护措施，”它说。

contentParagraphs.en: But few in the open source community seemed reassured by Google's statements. For van Ess, the decision particularly stings because Google Earth has long been regarded as one of the best tools to verify information posted on social media.
contentParagraphs.zh: 但开源社区中几乎没有人对谷歌的声明感到放心。对于范·埃斯来说，这一决定尤其令人痛苦，因为谷歌地球长期以来一直被认为是验证社交媒体上发布的信息的最佳工具之一。

contentParagraphs.en: If Google continues to develop the AI tool, he said, it would mean that "the fake is made inside the thing people use to check whether pictures are true."
contentParagraphs.zh: 他说，如果谷歌继续开发人工智能工具，这将意味着“人们用来检查图片是否真实的东西里会出现假货。”

articles.title: Thames Water boss says leakage targets 'not realistic'
articles.summary: Chris Weston said Thames wanted "to do better" but some of its targets were not achievable.
articles.titleZh: 泰晤士水务公司老板表示泄漏目标“不现实”
articles.summaryZh: 克里斯·韦斯顿表示，泰晤士河希望“做得更好”，但其中一些目标无法实现。

contentParagraphs.en: Water companies have performance commitments on issues such as leakage. It is illegal to release raw sewage into rivers and seas during "normal" weather conditions, but firms are allowed to do so when it rains heavily, to prevent homes being flooded.Thames is the UK's largest water company, supplying water and wastewater services to 16 million customers across London and parts of southern England.Speaking to the BBC's Big Boss Interview podcast, Weston said the company treats 4.3 billion litres of waste a day, and "99.5% of the time" it gets treated successfully, although "sometimes something goes wrong"."We want to do better when it comes to pollutions," he said, but added, "the targets that the company is expected to make are not realistic."[For example], we have to hit a certain level of leakage, but it is so far in excess of what we are capable of doing, I think anyone would be capable of doing, however much money you invested, that it is not going to be achievable."The chance of getting to zero pollution was "very, very slim", he added.Ofwat told the BBC: "With around a fifth of water put into supply still lost through leakage, companies must deliver on the commitments they have been funded to achieve."Water company targets are intended to be ambitious and drive better outcomes for customers and the environment."A spokesperson for the Environment Agency said: "[We] and the public expect Thames Water to comply with the law," adding that the agency would continue to hold companies to account where performance falls short.James Wallace, chief executive of campaign group River Action, said: "Thames Water's tactics of opacity and deflection fool no-one. Telling the public to save water while this wasteful profit-obsessed corporation leaks 570 million litres of treated drinking water every day is offensive. "There is nothing 'realistic' about accepting sewage pollution as inevitable. The choice is simple: keep propping up a failed privatised financial model, or put Thames Water into special administration and rebuild it as a public utility serving customers, rivers and the public."
contentParagraphs.zh: 自来水公司对渗漏等问题有绩效承诺。在“正常”天气条件下，将未经处理的污水排入河流和海洋是违法的，但在大雨时，公司可以这样做，以防止房屋被洪水淹没。泰晤士报业是英国最大的自来水公司，为伦敦和英格兰南部部分地区的 1600 万客户提供供水和废水处理服务。韦斯顿在接受 BBC 的 Big Boss Interview 播客时表示，该公司每天处理 43 亿升废物，“99.5% 的废物” “我们希望在污染方面做得更好，”他说，但又补充道，“公司预期制定的目标并不现实。”[例如]，我们必须达到一定程度的泄漏，但这远远超出了我们的能力范围，我认为任何人都有能力做到，无论你投入多少钱，这都是不可能实现的。“实现零污染的机会是他补充说，“非常非常渺茫”。 Ofwat 告诉 BBC：“大约五分之一的供水仍然因泄漏而损失，公司必须兑现他们已获得资金实现的承诺。”水务公司的目标旨在雄心勃勃，为客户和环境带来更好的结果。“环境署发言人表示：“[我们]和公众期望泰晤士水务局遵守法律，”并补充说，该机构将继续追究绩效不佳的公司的责任。该活动首席执行官詹姆斯·华莱士河流行动组织表示：“泰晤士水务公司的不透明和偏转策略骗不了任何人。告诉公众节约用水，而这家浪费性的、痴迷于利润的公司每天泄漏 5.7 亿升经过处理的饮用水，这是令人反感的。”接受污水污染不可避免是不现实的。选择很简单：继续支撑失败的私有化金融模式，或者将泰晤士水务纳入特殊管理，并将其重建为服务客户、河流和公众的公用事业。”

articles.title: Russian strikes on Kyiv kill at least nine, Ukraine officials say
articles.summary: The attack comes as Moscow escalates deadly ballistic missile attacks on the Ukrainian capital.
articles.titleZh: 乌克兰官员称，俄罗斯对基辅的袭击造成至少九人死亡
articles.summaryZh: 这次袭击发生之际，莫斯科正在升级对乌克兰首都的致命弹道导弹袭击。

contentParagraphs.en: At least nine people have been killed in Russian ballistic missile strikes on Kyiv, local officials said.A further 28 people were injured in the attack on the Ukrainian capital on Saturday morning, according to the country's State Emergency Service.Moscow has escalated deadly ballistic missile attacks on Kyiv recently, prompting Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky to say that missile interceptors are urgently needed.The strikes come two days after a suspected Russian cruise missile landed in Poland during a widespread attack on Ukraine that killed at least eight people, including six members of one family.Kyiv's Mayor Vitali Klitschko said the capital had come under a ballistic missile attack on Saturday, with AFP reporting more than 10 explosions. Fires broke out across the city and power cuts were reported in some areas.Klitschko said a residential building in Shevchenkivskyi was partially destroyed, trapping people inside. The emergency services said at least seven people were killed in a strike in the Darnytskyi district. Another 14 were injured, including two children, it reported.In Solomyanskyi district, two people died and eight were injured, including two children, as a five-storey residential building was partially destroyed, officials said.A missile landed near the Lithuanian embassy, breaking windows and scattering debris in the compound, Lithuania's foreign ministry said.
contentParagraphs.zh: 当地官员称，俄罗斯对基辅的弹道导弹袭击已造成至少 9 人死亡。据乌克兰国家紧急服务部门称，周六上午对乌克兰首都的袭击造成 28 人受伤。莫斯科最近升级了对基辅的致命弹道导弹袭击，促使乌克兰总统弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基表示迫切需要导弹拦截器。两天前，一枚疑似俄罗斯巡航导弹在一次大规模袭击中降落在波兰。乌克兰造成至少 8 人死亡，其中包括 1 个家庭的 6 名成员。 基辅市长维塔利·克里琴科 (Vitali Klitschko) 表示，首都周六遭到弹道导弹袭击，法新社报道称发生了 10 多起爆炸。全市爆发火灾，部分地区停电。克里琴科说，舍甫琴基夫斯基的一栋住宅楼部分被毁，有人被困在里面。紧急服务部门表示，达尔尼茨基地区的一次罢工至少造成七人死亡。据报道，另有 14 人受伤，其中包括两名儿童。官员称，在索洛米扬斯基区，一栋五层住宅楼部分被毁，造成两人死亡、八人受伤，其中包括两名儿童。立陶宛外交部称，一枚导弹落在立陶宛大使馆附近，砸碎了窗户，碎片散落在大使馆内。
